processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The steel was casted using a vacuum induction furnace.
Ingot heated at 1150 °C for 2 h before hot forging.

processing_steps.method: hot forging to rods with a section plane of 35 mm × 70 mm × 100 mm, followed by air cooling to room temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot forged to rods of section plane 35 mm × 70 mm × 100 mm.
Ingot homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h before hot rolling.

processing_steps.cooling_medium: water quenched to 550 °C, followed by air cooling to room temperature
processing_steps.method: hot rolled to 3 mm thickness steel sheet through 6 passes; start rolling temperature 1150 °C, finish rolling temperature 850 °C
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled to 3 mm sheet in 6 passes; subsequent water quench to 550 °C then air cooling to RT.

processing_steps.method: solution treatment at 900 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Defines sample H90; solution treatment experiments performed at 700–1000 °C for 1 h; specimens treated at 900 °C are referred to as H90.

microstructure_list.morphology: Equiaxed; present as blocky grains at ferrite triple-junction boundaries and lath-like grains between ferrite laths/embedded in ferrite grains

phases_present.morphology: Large amount of strip ferrite (termed α-ferrite to distinguish from δ-ferrite)
Changed from strip shape into fine blocky/equiaxed shape

structures.overall_structure: Duplex/multiphase microstructure consisting mainly of α-ferrite, δ-ferrite and austenite after solution treatment at 900 °C for 1 h; the morphology of δ-ferrite changed from strip shape into fine blocky shape and the austenite volume fraction increased to 33.8%.

grain_structure.texture: Small-angle grain boundaries increase with strain: 26% (ε=0.03), 31% (0.10), 45% (0.20), 51% (0.27)

phases_present.morphology: Blocky austenite predominantly at triple-junction boundaries (present at ε=0.03) and lath-like austenite between ferrite laths/inside ferrite grains; blocky grains disappear progressively, at ε=0.27 almost all retained austenite is lath-like
lath/needle-shaped; formed by strain-induced martensitic transformation of austenite
phases_present.volume_fraction: increases with strain (poor band contrast in EBSD; no absolute fraction given at each strain)
